With regard to your intertwined queries 2, 3, and 4, this Department will collectively address the same. It is important to note that as a barangay, the Mayor does not possess the authority to divest you of your responsibilities as the primary planning and implementing unit of government policies, plans, programs, and activities within the community, nor can these responsibilities be transferred to private entities. This is in consonance to Section 17 (a) of the LGC which pertinently provides that the local government units shall endeavor to be self-reliant and shall continue exercising the powers and discharging the duties and functions currently vested upon them. They shall also discharge the functions and responsibilities of national agencies and offices devolved to them. Local government units shall likewise exercise such other powers and discharge such other functions and responsibilities as are necessary, appropriate, or incidental to efficient and effective provisions of the basic services and facilities enumerated herein. One of the basic services and facilities included in the barangay is specified in Item (vi) (I) Section 17 of the LGC, viz: Infrastructure facilities such as multi-purpose hall, multipurpose pavement, plaza, sports center, and other similar facilities. Relatively, in DILG Opinion No. 13, series of 2020, this Department opined that the Day Care Center and any infrastructure facilities related to it, such as a perimeter fence around the lot intended for the barangay, is well within the power of a barangay as a local government unit. As a power expressly granted by the LGC, it may be exercised without unnecessary hindrance. The same applies to multipurpose buildings designated for the barangay, as these facilities are explicitly included in item (vi) of the LGC. Thus, it cannot be unjustifiably removed given that you are the primary implementing LGU tasked with fulfilling responsibilities to your constituents within the barangay. Finally, this opinion is based solely on the facts and representations as narrated from your letter and our appreciation of the same, without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have assisted you on this matter. ATTY. ROMEO P. ENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLNRPB/LLLS-LLRALD/mag page 2 of 2
